issue.body:
I am investigating PyTorch correctness issues relevant to stateful simulation loops. I asked Codex to re-evaluate this behavior against current `main` and existing unmerged PRs. After reviewing the narrowed scope and its relationship to #184164, I decided to report it because the first compiled invocation can appear correct while leaving persistent state stale, after which later invocations silently return wrong results.

AI assistance disclosure: Codex prepared and executed the reproducer and drafted the technical analysis quoted below. I reviewed the narrowed analysis before submitting it.

> ## Bug
>
> In inference, `torch.while_loop` permits `cond_fn` and `body_fn` to mutate captured tensors that are not carried inputs. With Python sources at current `main`, Inductor fails to replay a `cond_fn`-only mutation to external storage when the captured tensor was already updated before entering the loop.
>
> https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e4d9b6187e6ef2635cc2b648fbb409d25d6a9d9a/torch/_higher_order_ops/while_loop.py#L136-L209
>
> Eager and `aot_eager` preserve the mutation. Inductor updates the internal functional tensor, so the first call's returned clone is correct, but leaves the external tensor at the value immediately before the HOP (`0.8` on the first call). A second call then starts from that stale value and silently produces wrong numerical results.
>
> ## Reproducer
>
> ```python
> import torch
>
>
> def f(state):
>     state.mul_(0.8)
>
>     def cond(i, acc):
>         state.mul_(0.5)
>         return i < 2
>
>     def body(i, acc):
>         return i + 1, acc + state
>
>     i, acc = torch.while_loop(
>         cond,
>         body,
>         (
>             torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64),
>             torch.zeros_like(state),
>         ),
>     )
>     return i, acc, state.clone()
>
>
> def run(backend):
>     torch._dynamo.reset()
>     state = torch.ones((), dtype=torch.float64)
>     fn = f if backend == "eager" else torch.compile(
>         f, backend=backend, fullgraph=True
>     )
>
>     results = []
>     with torch.inference_mode():
>         for _ in range(2):
>             output = fn(state)
>             results.append(
>                 (
>                     tuple(item.item() for item in output),
>                     state.item(),
>                 )
>             )
>     print(backend, results)
>
>
> for backend in ("eager", "aot_eager", "inductor"):
>     run(backend)
> ```
>
> Each result is `(returned_values, external_state_after_call)`:
>
> ```text
> eager [
>   ((2, 0.6000000000000001, 0.1), 0.1),
>   ((2, 0.06000000000000001, 0.010000000000000002), 0.010000000000000002)
> ]
> aot_eager [
>   ((2, 0.6000000000000001, 0.1), 0.1),
>   ((2, 0.06000000000000001, 0.010000000000000002), 0.010000000000000002)
> ]
> inductor [
>   ((2, 0.6000000000000001, 0.1), 0.8),
>   ((2, 0.4800000000000001, 0.08000000000000002), 0.6400000000000001)
> ]
> ```
>
> The same failure occurs under `torch.no_grad()`. It also reproduces when the condition is false on its first evaluation: eager persists the mutation made by that one `cond_fn` call, whereas Inductor leaves external state at the pre-loop value even though `body_fn` never runs.
>
> ## Expected behavior
>
> Inductor should match eager and `aot_eager`: mutations of non-carried captured tensors made by `cond_fn` should be replayed to their external storage, including when the loop executes zero body iterations and across repeated compiled calls.
>
> ## Likely cause
>
> Dynamo already unions the storage mutations discovered in `cond_fn` and `body_fn` when constructing the higher-order operator:
>
> https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e4d9b6187e6ef2635cc2b648fbb409d25d6a9d9a/torch/_dynamo/variables/higher_order_ops.py#L932-L987
>
> In contrast, `torch._inductor.ir.WhileLoop.create` obtains mutation indices only from `body_fn`:
>
> ```python
> mutated_idxs = check_input_alias_and_mutation(
>     body_fn.graph.module, fake_all_inputs
> )[3]
> ```
>
> https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/e4d9b6187e6ef2635cc2b648fbb409d25d6a9d9a/torch/_inductor/ir.py#L11812-L11863
>
> Consequently, a captured additional input mutated only by `cond_fn` receives no `MutationOutput`/scheduler write dependency. A local prototype that unions the `cond_fn` and `body_fn` mutation indices, on top of the additional-input handling from #184164, fixes the nonzero-iteration, zero-iteration, and repeated-call cases above.
>
> ## Relationship to #184164
>
> #184164 is a closely related partial fix, not an exact duplicate. It fixes mutation replay for captured additional inputs mutated by `body_fn`. Applying that PR locally fixes the body-mutation reproducer but does not fix this `cond_fn`-only reproducer.
>
> The PR test's cond-mutated counter is lowered from an unchanged graph-input base, while a separate buffer is mutated in `body_fn`; it therefore does not exercise a computed functionalization base mutated only by `cond_fn`. This issue can likely be handled by extending #184164 to collect mutation indices from both subgraphs and adding the two regression boundaries above.
>
> Related issue: #182036
>
> ## Versions
>
> - Python sources: current `main` at `e4d9b6187e6ef2635cc2b648fbb409d25d6a9d9a`
> - Native extension build used with that source tree: `2.15.0a0+gitb3632e5` (`b3632e56519f39da86e50fb0aa27235d626e8306`)
> - Python: 3.12.3
> - OS: Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, x86_64
> - CPU: Intel Core i7-6700
> - `fullgraph=True`, CPU, `torch.inference_mode()`; CUDA was not involved

issue.body:
## Decision (2026-08-30)

The architecture decision is complete: adopt option 4 for the initial cutover by revising the CPU performance contract, while retaining the Torch-only/no-custom-C++ architecture.

- Native timing remains measured and published, but `<=1.05x` native is no longer a cutover blocker.
- The post-#145 Torch implementation rooted at master `821c075b9328e02c3f3e5d16488a44b64ff08c04` becomes the source of the complete corrected-runner CPU baseline. The hard timing gate is suite non-regression and no individual workload more than 5% slower than that baseline.
- Complete correctness and state progress, two intended static fullgraph regions, no warm graph break/recompilation/eager fallback/host conversion, and stable storage remain mandatory.
- Plan-bounded fixed-shape compiler temporaries are accepted temporarily when their generated-operation provenance, allocation counts/bytes, and peak/live memory are reported; link a public upstream report wherever one applies, and require no live-memory/RSS growth across repeated execution. Recurring full-field/domain clones remain prohibited.
- CUDA, two-GPU, workload-matrix, paired-real, profiler-evidence, and no-custom-C++ requirements are unchanged.

The parent contracts are amended in #114, #123, and #124. Upstream-triggered cleanup and performance requalification are registered in:

- #162 — pytorch/pytorch#195285: retire the direct-view mutation workaround;
- #163 — pytorch/pytorch#195327: reassess DM2 functional state flow;
- #164 — pytorch/pytorch#195329: requalify arena/live-view alias execution;
- #165 — pytorch/pytorch#195330: simplify indexed-update workspaces.

These are non-blocking post-cutover maintenance and start only after a fixed upstream change is available in a GMES-supported PyTorch build. PyTorch #195305 is not included because it is a contributor-tooling issue with no GMES runtime workaround or performance effect.

This decision unblocks #123 to finish the revised full matrix. It does not itself mark #123 complete or authorize #124 to start before that matrix passes.



---

## Parent and blocking relationship

Follow-up required by #123. This decision blocks completion of #123 and therefore the Torch-only cutover in #124.

## Decision needed

Choose how to satisfy the fixed CPU mixed-material contract while retaining the no-custom-C++ guarantee. The standard PyTorch 2.13/Inductor implementation now has only two static fullgraph calls per step, but remains far outside the frozen native limit. #123 explicitly forbids weakening or reclassifying this gate.

## Minimized project reproducer

The smallest frozen failing gate is `cpu-crossover-2d` at one thread. The reproducer and strict profiler runner are in commit [`2996271`](https://github.com/ruddyscent/gmes/commit/2996271c50f153c448884961f5330402a01a5b67):

```sh
uv sync --locked --extra torch-cpu --extra hdf5
uv run --no-sync python -m benchmarks.torch_tuning \
  --case cpu-crossover-2d --device cpu --precision float64 \
  --compile-mode default --policy auto --threads 1 --interop-threads 1 \
  --warmup 1 --steps 50 --repeats 5 --profile-steps 2 \
  --native-summary /tmp/gmes-native-v4-baseline-summary.json \
  --trace-directory /tmp/gmes-123-cpu-traces \
  --output /tmp/gmes-123-cpu.json --enforce
```

Expected result: exit status 2. The steady-state trace contains two compiled regions, zero graph breaks, zero recompilations, and zero host transfers, but reports recurring CPU allocations and misses the native timing gate.

## Measured evidence

Host: Intel i7-6700, 4 physical/8 logical cores; Python 3.14.7; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu126; float64. Frozen reference: `native-oracle-observer-v4`.

| Fixed case | Threads | Native ms/step | Torch ms/step | Torch/native |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| cpu-crossover-2d | 1 | 0.849 | 3.743 | 4.41x |
| cpu-crossover-2d | 4 | 0.666 | 3.227 | 4.85x |
| cpu-crossover-3d | 1 | 9.544 | 59.525 | 6.24x |
| cpu-crossover-3d | 4 | 6.797 | 34.746 | 5.11x |

The 2-D forced-policy matrix measured auto at 4.12 ms/step, compact at 4.36, tiled at 4.35, and dense at 4.54; auto is already the fastest candidate. The 3-D profiler attributes about 39.0 ms and 19.1 ms to the electric and magnetic compiled graphs themselves. Dispatch, graph breaks, recompilation, host polling, and planner choice have therefore been eliminated as primary causes. `cpp_wrapper=True` was also slower than the default wrapper.

For comparison, the same code passes the accelerator contracts: RTX 3060 large mixed 3-D is 2.90 ms/step with explicit graph capture (about 9.43x the same-host four-core native throughput); two-GPU strong scaling is 1.99x and weak efficiency is 111%.

## Options and trade-offs

1. **Wait for or contribute an upstream Inductor CPU improvement.** Expected benefit must be at least 4.4-6.2x on indexed mixed-material half-step graphs. Maintenance cost in GMES stays low and the no-C++ guarantee is preserved, but #123/#124 remain blocked until a released PyTorch build demonstrates the gate.
2. **Create a specialized non-C++ backend experiment.** A candidate must remain PyTorch-backed, support float64 and paired-real Bloch, preserve every material equation, and demonstrate at least the measured 4.4-6.2x recovery before adoption. Handwritten Triton is not an immediate CPU solution; adding a second JIT such as Numba would add substantial packaging/runtime maintenance and weaken the PyTorch-only contract. This option requires a separate prototype and explicit architecture approval.
3. **Retain or add a native CPU kernel.** Expected performance recovery is the observed 4.4-6.2x, but maintenance remains high and this directly violates both the no-custom-C++ guarantee and #124, so it is not eligible without changing the epic contract.
4. **Relax the CPU gate.** No implementation maintenance and preserves no-C++, but contradicts the hard acceptance criteria and is not an implementation decision #123 can make autonomously.

## Recommended disposition

Keep #123 and #124 blocked, preserve the profiler/reproducer branch, and pursue option 1 unless the epic owner explicitly authorizes a scoped prototype under option 2 or changes the contract. Do not merge the current branch as a completed #123 implementation: the CPU timing and recurring-allocation gates are demonstrably unmet.

issue.body:
## Parent

Post-cutover maintenance from #135 and #123. Blocked by the upstream correctness fix for [pytorch/pytorch#195327](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/195327) being available in a supported stable PyTorch release.

## Current safety boundary

GMES avoids captured mutable DM2 state across `torch.while_loop`: loop state is passed explicitly and returned functionally, with a packed CPU carry for the compiled path. This was introduced to preserve persistent state across repeated compiled calls after the DM2 re-audit.

The upstream report is narrower than the whole GMES state-flow design, so its resolution does not by itself prove that all explicit carries can be removed.

## Work

- Re-run the upstream nonzero-iteration, zero-body-iteration, and repeated-call reproducers on the supported fixed release.
- Prototype the smallest DM2 simplification permitted by the fixed captured-mutation semantics; compare it with the current functional and packed paths.
- Verify complete fields, DM2 `u`, status, iteration count, error behavior, time dependence, nonconvergence, and invalid-result handling after 1, 2, 5, 20, and 100 steps.
- Cover eager/compiled CPU, paired-real exclusions, repeated `advance()` calls, and all supported dtypes; retain CUDA behavior unchanged.
- Measure allocation histograms, live memory/RSS, compiled-region stability, and latency before deciding whether any carry/workspace code is redundant.

## Acceptance criteria

- Eager, compiled, and native-oracle state comparisons pass at the established tolerances, including zero-iteration and repeated-call boundaries.
- There are no graph breaks, recompilations, eager fallbacks, host conversions, stale external state, or unbounded memory growth.
- The simplified implementation has no statistically meaningful suite regression and no individual case more than 5% slower than the accepted Torch CPU baseline.
- Only workaround code demonstrably covered by the released upstream fix is removed; broader explicit state flow remains if it is still required for correctness or performance.

issue.title: fix(torch): reassess DM2 functional state workaround after PyTorch #195327

issue.body:
Stack from [ghstack](https://github.com/ezyang/ghstack/tree/0.17.0) (oldest at bottom):
* __->__ #195393

Fixes #195327

In inference mode, torch.while_loop allows cond_fn and body_fn to
mutate captured tensors that are not carried inputs. Inductor failed to
replay a cond_fn-only mutation to external storage when the captured
tensor was mutated before entering the loop: the first compiled call
returned correct values but left the external tensor stale, and later
calls silently produced wrong results.

Root cause: after AOT, the loop is wrapped as
auto_functionalized_v2(while_loop, ..., _all_bases=[...]) where the
base of the pre-mutated captured tensor is a computed intermediate,
with a copy_ epilogue writing back to the graph input. Inductor's
post-grad decomposition back to a plain while_loop does not carry
mutation metadata on the node, so WhileLoop.create re-derives it with
check_input_alias_and_mutation -- but only scanned body_fn, and only
registered MutationOutput for carried inputs (an unreachable "only
carries can be mutated" assertion guarded the additional-input case).
With no MutationOutput, the scheduler treated the loop as a pure reader
of the base buffer and fused the copy-back into the pre-loop kernel,
writing the stale pre-loop value into the user's tensor.

The fix unions mutated input indices from both cond_fn and body_fn
(the same pattern the Switch/cond lowering uses across branches) and
registers a MutationOutput for each mutated additional input so
outer-graph reads are ordered after the loop. It also replaces a
latent iterator/index mispairing for mutated carried inputs
(check_input_alias_and_mutation returns indices in graph-node order,
not ascending order) with direct all_inputs[idx] indexing. An
alternative of plumbing mutated_arg_indices through the
auto_functionalized_v2 decomposition was rejected: the v2 schema drops
that kwarg by design, and the subgraphs' copy_ nodes are the ground
truth at lowering time. The stack_output (training) path is unaffected
because functionalization rejects subgraph input mutations there.

Test Plan:

New device-generic regression tests (CPU+CUDA) covering cond/body/both
mutation of a pre-mutated captured tensor, the zero-iteration case, and
repeated compiled calls; all 18 instantiations fail before the fix and
pass after:

```
python test/functorch/test_control_flow.py -k "pre_mutated"
```

Targeted existing suites, all passing:

```
python test/functorch/test_control_flow.py -k "auto_functionalize"
python test/functorch/test_control_flow.py -k "while_loop"
python test/inductor/test_control_flow.py -k "while"
```

Lint:

```
lintrunner -a torch/_inductor/ir.py test/functorch/test_control_flow.py
```

Authored with an AI assistant (Claude Code).

subject.title: [inductor] Replay cond_fn mutations of captured tensors in while_loop

issue.body:
I re-reviewed the updated PR and reproduced the `cpp_wrapper` failure. The new test makes carried-input mutation depend on an unrelated captured-tensor mutation, contradicting the documented contract.

> [AI-assisted analysis]
>
> ## Bug
>
> `torch.while_loop` documents that `cond_fn` and `body_fn` must not mutate carried inputs in place, while captured non-carried tensors may be mutated during inference:
>
> https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fc660a81ddb088588f79920decaa9aabe7734cb7/torch/_higher_order_ops/while_loop.py#L192-L203
>
> The validation bypass predates #195393. It became reachable through inference-mode auto-functionalization added in #175972 (`b4a62e6df37004052d4b81715e1391ff93c0ce9f`).
>
> #195393 did not create the validation bypass. It made `cond_fn` mutations participate in Inductor mutation outputs, exposing a new C++ wrapper failure, and added a success test for the invalid mixed-mutation program.
>
> ## Why validation is bypassed
>
> Dynamo traces carried tensors using clones. A carried-input mutation alone is therefore not recovered in the parent `mutated_arg_indices`. The HOP schema remains functional, auto-functionalization does not run, and `_check_alias_and_mutation` rejects the mutation.
>
> If the same callback also mutates a parent-visible captured or additional tensor, that mutation makes the HOP schema mutable. `while_loop_func` then returns through auto-functionalization before `_check_alias_and_mutation` runs:
>
> https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fc660a81ddb088588f79920decaa9aabe7734cb7/torch/_higher_order_ops/while_loop.py#L621-L653
>
> The reproductions below pre-mutate the captured tensor to match #195327, but that pre-mutation is not required for the validation bypass. A captured or additional mutation that makes the schema mutable is sufficient.
>
> ## Reproducer
>
> Save as `repro.py`:
>
> ```python
> import torch
>
>
> def cond_case(y):
>     y.mul_(0.8)
>
>     def cond_fn(i, acc):
>         acc.mul_(0.99)
>         y.mul_(0.5)
>         return i < 2
>
>     def body_fn(i, acc):
>         return i + 1, acc + y
>
>     return torch.while_loop(
>         cond_fn,
>         body_fn,
>         (
>             torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64, device=y.device),
>             torch.zeros_like(y),
>         ),
>     )
>
>
> def body_case(y):
>     y.mul_(0.8)
>
>     def cond_fn(i, acc):
>         return i < 3
>
>     def body_fn(i, acc):
>         out = acc + 0.23
>         acc.zero_()
>         y.add_(1.0)
>         return i + 1, out
>
>     return torch.while_loop(
>         cond_fn,
>         body_fn,
>         (
>             torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64, device=y.device),
>             torch.zeros_like(y),
>         ),
>     )
>
>
> with torch.no_grad():
>     cond_out = torch.compile(
>         cond_case, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True
>     )(torch.ones(4))
>     eager_body = body_case(torch.ones(4))
>     compiled_body = torch.compile(
>         body_case, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True
>     )(torch.ones(4))
>
> print("cond:", cond_out)
> print("body eager:", eager_body[1])
> print("body compiled:", compiled_body[1])
> ```
>
> Run:
>
> ```shell
> python repro.py
> TORCHINDUCTOR_CPP_WRAPPER=1 python repro.py
> ```
>
> ## Observed behavior
>
> - Without the captured `y.mul_(0.5)` mutation in `cond_case`, carried-input mutation is rejected with `RuntimeError: cond_fn might be modifying the input!`.
> - With the captured mutation present, the default Python wrapper accepts `cond_case`.
> - With `cpp_wrapper=True`, the same program fails with:
>
> ```text
> InductorError: AssertionError: while_loop has unused non-mutated outputs
> ```
>
> - For `body_case`, eager returns the final carry value `0.69`, while default Inductor returns the stale value `0.0`.
>
> ## C++ wrapper failure
>
> For a carry mutated only by `cond_fn`, the lowering creates a regular `MultiOutput` because the carry is not in `body_mutated_idxs`. It also creates a `MutationOutput` because the carry is in the union of mutations from both callbacks:
>
> https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fc660a81ddb088588f79920decaa9aabe7734cb7/torch/_inductor/ir.py#L11835-L11867
>
> The C++ wrapper treats a `MutationOutput` corresponding to a carried input as replacing its regular carried output. The regular `MultiOutput` is therefore left unused:
>
> https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/fc660a81ddb088588f79920decaa9aabe7734cb7/torch/_inductor/codegen/cpp_wrapper_cpu.py#L2895-L2928
>
> ## Expected behavior
>
> Carried-input mutation should be rejected with a user-facing error regardless of:
>
> - whether a captured tensor is also mutated;
> - whether the mutation occurs in `cond_fn` or `body_fn`;
> - the selected Inductor wrapper.
>
> Validation should happen before auto-functionalization and backend-specific lowering. Regression tests should cover:
>
> - carried-input mutation in each callback, with and without captured mutation;
> - both Python and C++ wrappers;
> - continued support for captured-only mutation during inference.
>
> ## Regression scope
>
> - The validation bypass predates #195393 and is related to the inference mutation support added in #175972.
> - #195393 introduced the cond-side `MultiOutput`/`MutationOutput` conflict and added a success test for the invalid program.
> - The `body_fn` stale-result path predates #195393.
>
> ## Related
>
> - Follow-up to #195393
> - Related to #195327
> - Validation bypass originates from the inference mutation path added in #175972
>
>
> cc @chauhang @penguinwu @voznesenskym @EikanWang @jgong5 @Guobing-Chen @XiaobingSuper @zhuhaozhe @blzheng @wenzhe-nrv @jiayisunx @ipiszy @kadeng @muchulee8 @amjames @aakhundov @coconutruben @jataylo @ydwu4 @bdhirsh @bobrenjc93 @aorenste

issue.title: [inductor][while_loop] carried-input mutation validation is bypassed by auto-functionalization

issue.body:
I reviewed the AI-assisted analysis below against the reproducer and current source. I am filing it because `cond_fn` must be evaluated once even when it immediately returns `False`, and inference explicitly permits mutation of captured tensors.

> [AI-assisted analysis]
>
> ## Summary
>
> When `torch.while_loop`'s `cond_fn` returns the Python constant `False`, Dynamo short-circuits the loop and returns the carried operands without replaying mutations that `cond_fn` made to captured tensors.
>
> The loop body correctly runs zero times, but `cond_fn` itself should still run once. This is observable because captured-tensor mutation is explicitly supported during inference.
>
> ## Reproducer
>
> ```python
> import torch
>
>
> def f(state):
>     def cond_fn(i):
>         state.add_(1)
>         return False
>
>     def body_fn(i):
>         return (i + 1,)
>
>     return torch.while_loop(
>         cond_fn,
>         body_fn,
>         (torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.int64),),
>     )
>
>
> def run(name, fn):
>     state = torch.zeros(())
>     with torch.no_grad():
>         out = fn(state)
>     print(f"{name}: carry={out[0].item()}, captured={state.item()}")
>
>
> run("torch.while_loop", f)
> run("aot_eager", torch.compile(f, backend="aot_eager", fullgraph=True))
> run("inductor", torch.compile(f, backend="inductor", fullgraph=True))
> ```
>
> Output:
>
> ```text
> torch.while_loop: carry=0, captured=0.0
> aot_eager: carry=0, captured=0.0
> inductor: carry=0, captured=0.0
> ```
>
> `captured` should be `1.0` in every case because `cond_fn` is evaluated once before deciding that the body should not execute.
>
> Direct execution through `while_loop_op` produces the expected `captured=1.0`.
>
> ## Likely cause
>
> Dynamo [returns the original operands immediately](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/cea5123e28cb47f98fed03e49e5aeb79d0566419/torch/_dynamo/variables/higher_order_ops.py#L917-L930) when the speculative condition result is the Python constant `False`.
>
> That return happens before a `while_loop` HOP is constructed and before the captured condition mutation can be represented or replayed. In contrast, the dense implementation [evaluates `cond_fn` once before checking its result](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/cea5123e28cb47f98fed03e49e5aeb79d0566419/torch/_higher_order_ops/while_loop.py#L288-L302).
>
> ## Expected behavior
>
> Preserve the condition's permitted captured-tensor mutations when short-circuiting a constant-false loop, or avoid the shortcut when the captured condition graph has observable tensor mutations.
>
> ## Related issues
>
> This is distinct from #195327 / #195393, where a tensor-valued predicate reached the HOP and Inductor failed to replay a condition-only mutation. It is also distinct from #195966, which concerns validation of prohibited carried-input mutations.
>
> Confirmed against Python sources from `main` at `cea5123e28cb47f98fed03e49e5aeb79d0566419`.
